items.title: Steve Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 25, 2002
items.q: he told me about an instance when he was working with I think Albert Ayler or somebody like that.

ctx.x: I love that statement you just made in passing, and that was “I wasn’t thinking of anything when I wrote that.” I mean can you talk about that? Because I think it’s a very interesting thing and like you said I think sometimes we have to put a meaning on everything.

Yeah. I remember having a conversation about three years ago with Gary Peacock. We were both doing the Montreal Festival. And I had never met him before and I had a really fascinating conversation with him. I was very honored that he was talking to me. But he told me about an instance when he was working with I think Albert Ayler or somebody like that. And of course at that time they were being pegged the angry black musicians, because they’re playing avante garde or so-called avante garde. And Albert had read…
Yeah. When you write, are you getting to get more of your own tunes on records and so forth?
